interpretation_rules: Never compare PDMS and EPDMS as if they were identical.
Do not compare adapted Bench2Drive-220 results to full leaderboard results without matching routes, inputs, permitted data, controllers, and deployment rules.
Do not compare HUGSIM public aggregator results with paper zero-shot scores until split and evaluation scope match.
Keep world-model prediction, planner score, closed-loop driving, multi-agent realism, and decision-quality evidence as separate tracks.
Bench2Drive 0.0.3 rows are self-reported results copied from papers and vary by data, expert, training and inference compute; ground-truth-perception rows are privileged and must be separated.
Do not treat the 90.2 DriveVLA-W0 one-camera PDMS row and its separate dagger-marked 93.0 entry as the same configuration.
PlanWAM and World4Scorer both use K=64 candidate configurations; the EGCI selector reproduction ladder must include K=64 and charge generation, scoring, continuation and replay costs separately.

ReWAM is an existing reciprocal-response architecture; EGCI must not claim to invent reciprocal planning. Its contribution is independently verifiable execution, support-qualified counterfactual evaluation and evidence-audited decision quality.

The 2026-11-06 Bench2Drive 0.0.3 leaderboard lists TFv6+ScaleDrive 96.65 DS / 90.45 SR above BridgeDrive 96.34 / 89.25 in the non-privileged section; keep both separate from ground-truth-perception privileged rows.
FPD-Drive-Pro 58.07 EPDMS and DriveZero-Scale 57.1 EPDMS are NAVSIM-v2 navhard results. Never place them on the NAVSIM-v2 navtest line beside NTR/PlanWAM/World4Scorer.

NAVSIM-v1 and v2 are pseudo-closed-loop/open-loop scoring protocols, not fully reciprocal live traffic. NAVSIM docs describe v1 as a four-second non-reactive simulation with logged future actors and LQR ego control; v2 adds precomputed follow-up scenes.
DriveZero-Scale's NAVSIM-v1 row uses camera inputs, while its paper's human-driver reference uses ground-truth symbolic inputs; do not call that a matched human comparison.
DriveZero-Scale's HUGSIM 46.6 HD-Score is true closed-loop and zero-shot; it is strongest on Easy/Medium/Hard but not Extreme. Retain the tier breakdown and route completion.
NTR's 94.1 PDMS and 90.9 EPDMS are navtest rows; its 8.0461 Waymo E2E RFS and token effective-rank diagnostics are separate metrics/tracks.
FPD-Drive teacher future observations are training-only; deployed student uses current four-camera views, ego history and nav command without teacher inference.

The official Bench2Drive leaderboard README was last updated 24 Sep 2026. TFv6+ScaleDrive 96.65 / 90.45 is from the ScaleDrive paper Table 5 dated 2 Nov 2026, not the official leaderboard README; keep a separate bench2drive_paper track.
ScaleDrive is action-free representation pretraining, not an interactive policy or evidence-qualified counterfactual method. Compare it on exact planner, data, sensor and compute protocol.

SparseWAM reports 92.6 PDMS / 90.1 EPDMS using a 16-register representation and 64 sampled trajectories; its 164ms latency is measured on an NVIDIA H20 at batch 1 and cannot be transferred to another device.
NAVSIM-v1 PDMS, NAVSIM-v2 navtest EPDMS and NAVSIM-v2 NavHard EPDMS are different tracks; values must never be ordered across tracks.
